issuingEntity: unknown. No token document names a legal issuing entity. The only legal entity any primary source names is Step Labs LLC, which the 2026 remoramarkets.xyz Privacy Policy defines as "Remora Markets", "we" or "us" — the operator of the website and service — without giving its state or country of organisation, a registered address, a registration number, or any statement that it issued the rTokens. The platform was 'formerly Moose Capital', acquired by Step Finance in December 2024 and rebranded; Step Finance said it had integrated Moose Capital's team and regulatory licences, and the 2026 About page names the acquirer as 'Step Foundation'. The 2025 remora.markets site never named a company, and its Terms & Conditions, Whitepaper, KYC Info and Privacy Policy pages were published as empty stubs (verified in the Wayback captures of 2025-05-16); the 2026 site at remoramarkets.xyz listed four legal pages in its sitemap and footer menu (Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, Disclaimer, Service Providers; sitemap lastmod 2026-01-16), and only the Privacy Policy was ever archived with content: the Wayback Machine holds no capture of the Terms of Use, and its only captures of the Disclaimer and Service Providers pages (2026-03-11 and 2026-04-16) are redirects to the site's /not-available region-block page; archive.today holds nothing for the domain. Note: 'Remora Capital Corporation' (Maryland, SEC CIK 2045370) is a middle-market credit BDC and is NOT related, and nothing connects Step Labs LLC to the London-addressed 'Step Labs XYZ' of steplabs.xyz.
entityJurisdiction: unknown. The one named entity, Step Labs LLC (the 2026 Privacy Policy's "Remora Markets"), is given no state or country of organisation and no address; the 'LLC' suffix is used by every US state and by several offshore registries, so it does not locate the company, and neither SEC EDGAR full-text search nor the GLEIF LEI register returns any entity of that name (2026-09-23). The 2025 About page claimed only an 'Asset management license in premium offshore jurisdictions' and that 'Custodial services [are] managed by Wealth Management providers regulated in UAE'; secondary reporting says Remora was registered in Canada and the UAE. Circumstantial support for the UAE: app.remora.markets is a CNAME to mooseprodapialb-2015871155.me-central-1.elb.amazonaws.com — an AWS load balancer in the UAE (me-central-1) region, whose name preserves the 'Moose' origin. Re-checked 2026-09-18 against both 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8: the CNAME record itself is STILL published, so this piece of circumstantial UAE evidence remains checkable; it is the AWS target that no longer exists, which is why an A lookup for app.remora.markets returns NXDOMAIN.
governingLaw: unknown — no readable source states one. The 2025 remora.markets /terms-conditions/ page existed but contained no terms; the 2026 remoramarkets.xyz Terms of Use existed (listed in the sitemap and legal menu, and invoked by the Privacy Policy) but no archive holds its text; the archived 2026 Privacy Policy names Step Labs LLC but states no governing law, forum or dispute clause.
regulatoryStatus: unknown / self-asserted only. Claimed an unnamed offshore asset-management licence and UAE-regulated custodial providers; no regulator, licence number, prospectus or exemption was ever published. The platform was not available to users in the United States or Europe pending approvals, and required KYB for business users. The 2026 site enforced a region block — "our services are currently not available in your region due to regulatory requirements" — and its Privacy Policy said Step Labs LLC took no deliberate steps to direct the offering at individuals located in the USA or any other sanctioned or prohibited country; neither page names the regulation relied on.
holderClaim: Undocumented. In practice the holder held a platform-issued token that the operator asserted was backed 1:1 by the corresponding security or metal held through an unnamed regulated custodian, redeemable through the platform for USDC. No terms, prospectus or note conditions survive in any readable source — the 2025 legal pages were empty and the 2026 Terms of Use was never archived — so the legal nature, ranking and enforceability of the claim are unknown; the only contracting party a surviving document names is Step Labs LLC, as operator of the website. Post-wind-down the operator characterised it as a USDC redemption claim rather than a claim to the share.
underlyingCustodian: unknown — not named in any source that can still be read. The 2025 About page said only 'Custodial services managed by Wealth Management providers regulated in UAE'; the 2026 site at remoramarkets.xyz said each tokenized equity is 'held through a regulated custodian (see legal documentation)', and the Service Providers page of that legal documentation (remoramarkets.xyz/legal-documentation/service-providers) was never archived with content: the Wayback Machine's only two captures, 2026-03-11 and 2026-04-16, are redirects to the site's /not-available region block. A BitGo custody attribution sourced to https://remoramarkets.xyz/proof-of-reserves cannot be corroborated: that domain stopped resolving between 2026-08-14 (the last Wayback capture the host answered) and 2026-09-16 (the first failed check), and neither the Wayback Machine (476 captures of the domain, none of a proof-of-reserves path) nor archive.today holds a copy of the page (checked 2026-09-23). 'unknown' rests on the About page and on the absence of any naming source, not on the dead page, so it stands.

custodyVerification.frequency: Claimed 'Monthly Proof of Reserve audits' on the About page; no auditor named, no report ever located
custodyVerification.notes: No proof-of-reserve report, feed or oracle was found from any primary source. The only reserve figure the issuer ever displayed was its own 'CUSTODIED SHARES' column beside 'TOKEN SUPPLY' on the 2026 products page (Wayback capture of 2026-01-29; e.g. TSLAr 3,079 / 3,079), with no custodian, date or attestor. There is no Chainlink PoR feed, no attestation firm named, and no API. Post-wind-down the operator merely asserted that 'all rTokens are still fully backed at a 1:1 ratio' with no supporting evidence. The claim of monthly third-party PoR audits should be treated as unverified marketing, not an attestation.

redemption.eligibility: Originally: hold a Remora platform account (KYC for individuals, KYB for businesses); deposit USDC to mint, redeem through the platform. Post-wind-down: the operator said it was 'developing a redemption process for holders to exchange for USDC', and on 2026-03-02 deployed exit liquidity on Manifest DEX priced at the prior Friday's market close, reachable through the Jupiter and Titan swap routers — i.e. open to any token holder via a DEX rather than a contractual redemption right. Re-checked 2026-09-18: that route is gone too. Jupiter, the router the wind-down told holders to use, refuses to quote the rTokens at all (TOKEN_NOT_TRADABLE on TSLAr, GLDr, SPYr and CRCLr; NVDAr, which still answered NO_ROUTES_FOUND on 2026-09-18, answers TOKEN_NOT_TRADABLE too on the 2026-09-23 re-read), the Manifest exit book appears in no aggregator's pool list, and the only pools left are the original 2025 trading pools holding $13.47 across four TSLAr pools, $0.30 on GLDr and $1,040.51 on NVDAr at zero 24-hour volume except $370.99 on NVDAr/USDC. There is no redemption right, no redemption process and now no market: redemption.available is recorded false.
redemption.rails: Originally USDC on Solana (mint and redeem); post-wind-down, a DEX exit-liquidity pool on Manifest routed via Jupiter/Titan. As of 2026-09-18 no rail functions: Jupiter will not quote the mints and the residual Raydium pools hold double-digit dollars. Withdrawal of the token itself to self-custody still works, which is not a redemption rail.

knownExtensions: defaultAccountState (initialized — not frozen by default, no allowlist)
corporateActions: unknown. The mints carry the Token-2022 scaledUiAmountConfig extension — the same mechanism xStocks uses for rebasing dividends and splits — but the multiplier is 1 with no scheduled change on every mint inspected (TSLAr, NVDAr, GLDr), so no rebasing had ever been applied. No dividend, split or delisting policy was ever published.

pricing.notes: Minting was priced at 'the current price on traditional exchanges' per the platform's own How It Works page — a platform mark, with no named oracle. Arbitrage depended entirely on the platform's mint/redeem window being open to the arbitrageur, which required an account; that window is now closed. The wind-down exit liquidity was priced off the prior Friday's market close, i.e. a stale mark. Third-party valuations disagree THREE ways for the same platform within a day, across more than two orders of magnitude: CoinGecko's 'Remora Markets Tokenized rStocks' category reports a ~$138.9M aggregate market cap, RWA.xyz reported $1.87M distributed asset value on 17 September 2026 ($2.13M on 24 September), and DefiLlama reported $479,846 on 18 September ($296,074 on 24 September, after a one-day $2,834,038 data point dated 20 September). Nor is any one of them self-consistent: DefiLlama's own daily series records $0 on 42 days between 2026-07-02 and 2026-09-10 before returning to $479,846, and its own record has flagged the protocol dead since 2026-02-23 while it keeps publishing a daily figure. Treat all third-party valuation figures for these tokens as unreliable.

incidents.summary: Parent Step Finance was compromised: attacker access to executive-team devices allowed stake authority on treasury wallets to be transferred, and 261,854 SOL (~$28.9M at the time; ~$40M including fee wallets) was unstaked and moved out of the project's control. STEP fell roughly 96% over the following weeks. This was a parent-treasury compromise, not a compromise of the rToken mints or of customer collateral as far as reported.
incidents.quote: On January 31, 2026, Step Finance disclosed a critical security incident: attacker access to compromised devices belonging to executive team members allowed stake authorization to be transferred from the project's treasury wallets. A total of 261,854 SOL — worth approximately $28.9 million at the time of the theft — was unstaked and moved out of project control.

keyGovernance.evidence: Every rToken mint names the single key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb as mint, freeze, pause, permanent-delegate and metadata authority (RPC getAccountInfo on FJug3z58gssSTDhVNkTse5fP8GRZzuidf9SRtfB2RhDe and the other mints, 2026-09-16; re-verified 2026-09-17). Characterised 2026-09-17: that key is NOT a bare keypair but the Squads v4 vault PDA (vault index 0, bump 251) of multisig 7QsgDVkiM2285Mvi5TUf1gtHj1QzcqMyix6Rgrcqko35, which is owned by the Squads v4 program SQDS4ep65T869zMMBKyuUq6aD6EgTu8psMjkvj52pCf, has threshold 2 of 3 members, timeLock 0 and configAuthority 11111111111111111111111111111111 (no config authority, so membership and threshold are immutable), and had reached transactionIndex 640. Members: 4aog1ZhoEDrx47fddZ1BYq6yeXgb8mufTubJ3dvgLi6f (permissions 3), 7bzfFK9VxtUgK9Pr1mg7HegQtWPk9mXxmXkf556QMAEz (permissions 7), H61gpHmkSvTSLNWDuJvLA62EVtjrdfHDD5hF978pwa4E (permissions 6). Proof it is the vault and not a keypair: in tx 3wLDeSocn6Tg52KPjH3HWvohfpq9vVWoo8d9zXGLiSXd9L1h2BkpJtvYuET8KjurUuNMT1Ls1QEhRhrgsdGHy7Ts (2026-06-29) the Squads program logs 'Instruction: VaultTransactionExecute' and DQSTm2Wt... signs an inner SPL transferChecked as authority, which a transaction-level keypair signature does not do and a PDA can only do by CPI; the vault PDA derivation for index 0 also hashes to that address exactly. So all three powers sit behind a 2-of-3 multisig rather than one key, though the three member identities remain unattributed. The rebase (scaledUiAmountConfig) authority is DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb on all five rStock mints — the same single address that holds mint, freeze and permanent delegate — so it inherits their characterisation. Multiplier 1 everywhere: never used. RESOLVED 2026-09-18: the doubt raised on 2026-09-17 — that DQSTm2Wt... reads as a plain system-owned account (owner 11111111111111111111111111111111, space 0) holding 0.001995004 SOL, i.e. the shape of a hot key — does not survive the transaction evidence, and a system-owned zero-space account is also exactly what an uninitialised Squads v4 vault PDA looks like. Re-read 2026-09-18: multisig 7QsgDVkiM2285Mvi5TUf1gtHj1QzcqMyix6Rgrcqko35 is still owned by the Squads v4 program and 495 bytes long, and in tx 3wLDeSocn6Tg52KPjH3HWvohfpq9vVWoo8d9zXGLiSXd9L1h2BkpJtvYuET8KjurUuNMT1Ls1QEhRhrgsdGHy7Ts (2026-06-29T09:35:46Z) the ONLY transaction signer is member H61gpHmkSvTSLNWDuJvLA62EVtjrdfHDD5hF978pwa4E, the Squads program logs 'Instruction: VaultTransactionExecute', DQSTm2Wt... appears as a non-signer writable account, and the inner spl-token transferChecked names DQSTm2Wt... as its 'authority' — which a non-signing account can only be by PDA CPI. The multisig reading stands; the flag is cleared. What remains unknown is who the three members are.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: No legal documentation was ever published — the Terms & Conditions and Whitepaper pages were empty — so nothing establishes whether the chain or the operator's internal books was the authoritative record of entitlement. Evidence cuts both ways: minting and redemption ran through the platform's account system (suggesting an off-chain book), but the wind-down remedy was open DEX exit liquidity honouring whoever held the token (suggesting ledger state governed). Recorded as unknown rather than guessed.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Verified on Solana mainnet 2026-09-16 for TSLAr, NVDAr and GLDr: defaultAccountState = initialized (accounts are not frozen on creation, so no allowlist) and no transferHook extension at all. The platform itself advertised withdrawing rTokens to your own non-custodial wallet and using them across Solana DeFi. No gatekeeper approval was required for a transfer.

bearerRedemption.reason: Minting and redemption both ran through a Remora platform account subject to KYC (KYB for businesses); holding the token alone never entitled the bearer to the underlying. After the wind-down the only route out is a discretionary exit-liquidity pool on a DEX, priced off a stale mark — a courtesy, not a redemption right, and with no published terms there is nothing to enforce.

forcedTransfers.reason: Verified on-chain: every rToken mint carries a permanentDelegate, a freezeAuthority and a pausableConfig, all set to the single key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb (which is also mint authority, metadata update authority and scaledUiAmount authority). Whoever holds that key can move or burn any holder's tokens without consent. Concentration in one key is itself a risk given the parent's January 2026 device compromise.

titleDeed.reason: The token was marketed as economic exposure to a stock or metal held by a third-party custodian, not as the security itself. No shareholder rights, no register entry, no published instrument conveying ownership.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: The platform's How It Works page instructed users to 'Withdraw your RWAs to your own non-custodial wallet on Solana', and on-chain state confirms ordinary unfrozen Token-2022 accounts. Self-custody works and still works today.

issuerIndependent.reason: Demonstrated empirically, not merely inferred: the issuer wound down in February 2026 and the token's meaning collapsed with it. The web presence is gone (apex domain serves a cPanel placeholder, TLS expired 2026-03-06, alternate domain does not resolve), no proof of reserves is published, no redemption counterparty is contactable, and residual holders are left with a token whose backing rests on an undocumented assertion. The tokens still transfer, but they no longer reliably mean anything.

presetJurisdiction.reason: No governing law, forum or issuing entity was ever disclosed. The strongest published statement was 'Asset management license in premium offshore jurisdictions' with no jurisdiction, regulator or licence named, and the Terms & Conditions page was blank. A holder cannot determine which law governs the claim or where to bring it.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: 'Monthly Proof of Reserve audits' were claimed on the About page but no auditor was ever named, no report was ever published, and no feed or oracle existed. No independent attestation was attached to the token in any form. (The earlier rwa-sonar record asserting BitGo custody, sourced to remoramarkets.xyz/proof-of-reserves, is unsupported — that domain does not resolve.)

aiReady.reason: Per the vocabulary formula: unconditionalTransfers = yes and tokenSelfCustody = yes, so no KYC sits in the transfer loop and an agent could hold and trade rTokens. Largely academic now — with the issuer gone, there is nothing worth holding.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The on-chain mechanism exists (permanent delegate, freeze, pause) but no surviving document gives a governing law or forum, the one named company (Step Labs LLC) has no stated place of organisation, and no operator is still answering — so there is no route by which a court decision could be directed at anyone with the power to act on the ledger. Capability without an accountable holder of that capability is not enforceability.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Secondary transfers settled on the parties' agreement alone, with no issuer or platform sign-off, as verified by the absence of any transfer hook or allowlist on the mints.
